summary: Wooden lighthouse built on Lake Champlain's Colchester Reef in 1871; moved in 1952 to the Shelburne Museum, where it stands today.

lens.where: Shelburne Museum (Coast Guard gift, per LighthouseFriends)

structures.type: tower on a Second Empire dwelling
structures.note: Dismantled from the reef and rebuilt on the Shelburne Museum grounds in 1952.

access.note: On the Shelburne Museum grounds; the USLHS archive lists it as open to the public.

events.note: Wooden tower on a dwelling with a granite-pier foundation; built 1870-1871 by Luther Whitney to Albert R. Dow's design.
Violent January storm; lens thrown from its pedestal (LighthouseFriends); lens damaged (New England Lighthouses).
300 tons of riprap placed about the pier.
Riprap contract let and riprap placed to protect the foundation (fiscal year ended 30 June 1920).
Ice damage shown in a photograph dated April 1923 (New England Lighthouses caption).
Riprap work at the reef reported completed.
Light discontinued; battery-powered beacon fixed to the tower (LighthouseFriends).
Auctioned in June 1952 (LighthouseFriends); sold to Electra Webb. New England Lighthouses gives a different sequence.
Dismantled from the reef and rebuilt on the Shelburne Museum grounds.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A Colchester Reef in Lake Erie, Ontario, appears in Canadian reports under the same name. The Commissioner's 1920 report places this light at 'Colchester Reef Light Station, Lake Champlain', and the Canadian entries were excluded.

notes_for_editor: (1) Location: the record's point (44.375, -73.231) is the Shelburne Museum site; it matches the marker's coordinates (44 deg 22.517 min N, 73 deg 13.882 min W). The record does not give the original reef position. The USLHS place record gives 44 deg 33.5 min N, which is plausible for the reef, but its 72 deg 03 min W cannot be right for Lake Champlain; the roster tool flagged the place record's coordinates. A human should decide what 'location' means for a relocated light. (2) Height: the record's 10.7 m (35 ft) follows the USLHS 'height of light above mean high water'; LighthouseFriends gives a 51-foot focal plane (15.5 m). The story gives both. (3) Range: LighthouseFriends says 8 miles and New England Lighthouses says 11 miles; neither is in the record and neither is used. (4) Characteristic: LighthouseFriends and New England Lighthouses say fixed red; the record has none. Check the Light List history. (5) Lens: USLHS gives an original sixth-order lens; LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard gave the museum a Fresnel lens; New England Lighthouses says the original sixth-order lens remains in place. The facts object follows the Coast Guard gift wording and does not claim which lens is on display. (6) Keepers: the roster lists 20 lines and nine distinct principal keepers. The museum says eleven keepers; New England Lighthouses says nine. The last keeper is disputed: LighthouseFriends names Joseph Aubin (to August 1933); the roster ends with George Doig (Doige) (1931-1933) and lists no Aubin here; New England Lighthouses gives Aubin 1931-1933. Lorenz is 1909-1930 on the roster and 1909-1931 elsewhere. (7) Unverified: New England Lighthouses says an assistant keeper, Chandler McNeil, drowned on 21 May 1879 trying to help a disabled boat. The roster lists Harman C. McNall as assistant in 1879. Not linked and not in the story. (8) The 1952 transfer: LighthouseFriends describes a June 1952 auction, a $50 high bid by a young couple and a $1,300 purchase by Electra Webb plus materials; New England Lighthouses describes a $50 purchase from the Coast Guard and a July 1952 sale to Webb. Unresolved. The story states both. (9) The crew that moved it: the marker names six men (checked as printed on HMDB) and LighthouseFriends refers to a plaque for six men; New England Lighthouses says five men. The story states the disagreement. (10) Shape: the USLHS archive says square on dwelling; LighthouseFriends says an octagonal tower on a mansard roof in Second Empire style. (11) Primary sources: the Light-House Board reports of 1870-1890 are not in the local corpus (the corpus holds Lighthouse Board volumes for 1891-1901 only). The 1869 Board recommendation and the 1871 construction are read only as printed in LighthouseFriends or New England Lighthouses. (12) Fiscal years: the Commissioner's riprap passages are in the reports for the fiscal years ended 30 June 1920 (scan 543, printed 45) and 30 June 1922 (scan 742, printed 42); the 1921 report (scan 655) records the placing as completed. The 1930 Bulletin's fog minimum is for the fiscal year 1929. (13) The 1923 Bulletin riprap line was checked on the page image (PDF page 27): 'Work completed at Colchester Reef' reads clearly in the left column. The 1920 Bulletin line (PDF page 38) reads 'Work of placing riprap at Colchester Reef Light Station has been completed.' (14) Photos were not added.
